name: Can Tho to Ca Mau
summary: Take the new expressway. It opened in January 2026 and cut the ride to about an hour and a half, half the old three hours. Motorbikes cannot use it, so riders stay on the old road. The expressway stops short of Mũi Cà Mau; the cape is another road day from the city.

modes.note: About 111 km, from Cái Răng to the IC12 junction at Hồ Thị Kỷ. Opened to traffic on 19 January 2026. Speed limit 80 km/h. Tolls are collected non-stop; the amount is Check on arrival. No motorbikes, bicycles, or people on foot.
Buses run between the two cities. Times and fares are Check on arrival. Ca Mau’s coach station is on Lý Thường Kiệt; confirm the bay when you buy.
The ride took about three hours before the expressway opened. This is the road for motorbikes. A current timing is Check on arrival.

seoTitle: Can Tho to Ca Mau — expressway or bus
seoDescription: About 1.5 hours on the Cần Thơ–Cà Mau expressway, open since January 2026, against about three hours on the old road. Bus times are Check on arrival.

faqs.q: Does the expressway reach the Cà Mau cape?
faqs.a: No. It ends at the IC12 junction at Hồ Thị Kỷ. Đất Mũi is a separate road trip south, through Năm Căn.

faqs.q: Is there a train to Ca Mau?
faqs.a: No. The Mekong Delta has no passenger railway, and a planned line to Can Tho does not reach Ca Mau.
